'Scrap. When this attacks, IF IT SCRAPPED A CARD, this gets overpower.'

THE CONDITION WAS ALWAYS TRUE. It read HAS_KEYWORD "Scrap" -- whether the card PRINTS the keyword, which it always does -- rather than whether it actually scrapped anything when played. So the gate answered yes on every attack, and the printed Overpower applied unconditionally on top of it: two independent reasons the card always had overpower, neither visible to an audit, because both types are real and every parameter is read.

SCRAPPED (CR 8.3.32) is the condition that asks what the text asks. It is keyed by the card's own slug, matching the printed "IT scrapped" rather than "you scrapped", so another Mechanologist card scrapping this turn does not satisfy it.

Whether it scrapped is settled when the card is played and cannot change afterwards, so the WHILE_STATIC reading (CR 6.2.3d) gives the same answer as reading it once -- and that shape is what loader.conditional_keywords strips the printed keyword for.
